relevance_reason: The paper describes a family with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy caused by a heterozygous MPZ mutation (MPZ is the gene behind CHN2), seen in two generations and followed long term.

findings.statement: Smit et al. (2008) described a family with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy who carried a heterozygous mutation in the MPZ gene. The mutation was confirmed in two generations.
quotes: Here we describe a family with a heterozygous mutation in MPZ, confirmed in two generations.

findings.statement: Smit et al. (2008) noted that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition with prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis, and areflexia. On histopathology, myelin sheaths are absent or thin, and most reported patients have died within the first years of life. Mutations had been described in the MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2 genes.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition characterized by prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis and areflexia.
Histopathologically there are no or thin myelin sheaths.
Mutations have been described in the following genes, MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy and a novel MPZ mutation (Thr124Lys), directly relevant to CHN2 (MPZ-related).

findings.statement: Kochanski et al. (2004) described the clinical and morphologic features of a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN), a severe neuropathy with onset in early infancy. Sural nerve biopsy in CHN shows a characteristic picture of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and lack of myelin breakdown products.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN; MIM# 605253) is a severe neuropathy with early infancy onset
Sural nerve biopsy shows a characteristic picture of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and lack of myelin breakdown products.
The authors describe the clinical and morphologic features of a patient with CHN

phenotypes.text: severe neuropathy with early infancy onset
hypomyelinated axons on sural nerve biopsy

findings.statement: In a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, Kochanski et al. (2004) identified a novel thr124-to-lys (T124K) mutation in the MPZ gene.
quotes: The authors describe the clinical and morphologic features of a patient with CHN and the identification of a novel Thr124Lys mutation in the MPZ gene.

relevance_reason: Case report of congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy caused by a de novo MPZ frameshift mutation.

findings.statement: Szigeti et al. (2003) reported a patient with congenital hypomyelination associated with cranial nerve dysfunction, respiratory failure, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the latter confounding the clinical picture. Muscle biopsy findings suggested an effect of abnormal innervation on early postnatal muscle fiber differentiation.
quotes: We report a case of congenital hypomyelination associated with cranial nerve dysfunction, respiratory failure, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy confounding the clinical picture.
Muscle biopsy findings are presented that allude to the effect of abnormal innervation on early postnatal muscle differentiation.

phenotypes.text: abnormal muscle fiber differentiation on biopsy
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of skeletal muscle fiber size

findings.statement: In a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, Szigeti et al. (2003) identified a complex de novo mutation in the MPZ gene consisting of a 3-bp deletion of CTA from nucleotides 550 to 552 and insertion of G at nucleotide 550, predicted by conceptual translation to result in a frameshift.
quotes: Molecular genetic testing showed a complex de novo myelin protein zero (MPZ) mutation consisting of a 3bp deletion of CTA from nucleotide 550 to 552 and insertion of G at nucleotide 550 that by conceptual translation results in a frameshift mutation.

variants.as_reported: 3bp deletion of CTA from nucleotide 550 to 552 and insertion of G at nucleotide 550

relevance_reason: The paper reports a patient with congenital hypomyelination who carries a de novo MPZ mutation, Q215X. This directly supports CHN2 as an MPZ-related disorder.

findings.statement: Mandich et al. (1999) described the clinical, morphological, and immunohistochemical features of a patient with congenital hypomyelination. The authors characterized congenital hypomyelination as a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy with onset in early infancy, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severely slowed nerve conduction velocities. They reported that the patient's clinical features were quite distinct from those of CMT1B or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelination (CH) is a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities.
the clinical, morphological, and immunohistochemical features of a CH case

phenotypes.text: severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities

findings.statement: In a patient with congenital hypomyelination, Mandich et al. (1999) identified a de novo Q215X mutation in the MPZ gene, which encodes myelin protein zero (P0). The authors concluded that this finding confirms that congenital hypomyelination is allelic with milder MPZ-related disorders, namely CMT1B and Dejerine-Sottas syndrome.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelination due to myelin protein zero Q215X mutation.

This "de novo" mutation in a patient presenting with clinical features quite distinct from those of the more frequent Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 1B disease (CMT1B) or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS) confirms that CH is allelic

relevance_reason: The abstract reports new MPZ mutations in patients with congenital hypomyelination (CHN2), as well as in CMT1B and DSS.

findings.statement: Warner et al. (1996) identified 5 new mutations in the MPZ gene, which encodes the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin. The patients had CMT1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, or congenital hypomyelination.
quotes: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.

findings.statement: Warner et al. (1996) suggested that CMT1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, and congenital hypomyelination may not be separate pathophysiologic entities. They proposed instead that these disorders form a spectrum of related 'myelinopathies' caused by an underlying defect in myelination.
quotes: This finding suggests that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities, but rather represent a spectrum of related "myelinopathies" due to an underlying defect in myelination.

findings.statement: Warner et al. (1996) hypothesized that differences in clinical severity among MPZ mutations depend on the type of mutation and its effect on protein function, i.e., loss of function versus dominant-negative.
quotes: we hypothesize the differences in clinical severity seen with mutations in MPZ are related to the type of mutation and its subsequent effect on protein function (i.e., loss of function versus dominant negative).
